channel.title: Honda recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Honda CMX300, CMX500 Handlebar Lock Screw May Loosen
item.description: Certain Honda CMX300 and CMX500 motorcycles, along with the Honda SCL500, have a screw that locks the handlebar in place. This lock screw can loosen over time and detach completely. If the screw comes loose, it may lodge between the motorcycle's frame and the steering stem, getting in the way of how the handlebars turn. This recall expands an earlier Honda recall that covered the same handlebar lock screw issue.

item.title: Honda Odyssey rearview camera may fail from water entry
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Odyssey vehicles because water can get into the rearview camera. When that happens, the camera image may not show up on the screen when the vehicle is put in reverse. Because the image can fail to appear, these vehicles do not meet the federal rules for rear visibility. A dealer will replace the rearview camera at no cost to the owner. Honda mailed notification letters to owners and has a customer service line for questions.

item.title: Honda Hybrid Models: Tire Repair Kit Bottle Hazard
item.description: On some Accord Hybrid and CR-V Hybrid vehicles, using the tire repair kit can cause pressure to build inside the sealant bottle. That pressure can cause the bottle cap to detach while someone is using the kit.

item.title: Honda, Acura Rear Subframe May Corrode And Fail
item.description: On these vehicles, the rear subframe can corrode at the points where the suspension is mounted. If this happens, rear suspension parts, such as the rear control arm, can fail. This affects vehicles sold in a number of states. Dealers will inspect the rear subframe and install a reinforcement kit, and repair or replace subframe components as needed, free of charge. A final remedy is expected later, and additional letters will follow once it's ready.

item.title: Honda and Acura front passenger airbags may deploy unintentionally
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Honda and Acura vehicles, including the Accord, Civic, CR-V, Odyssey, Pilot, Ridgeline, HR-V, Fit, Insight, Passport and the Acura TLX, RDX and MDX. The sensor that measures the weight of the person in the front passenger seat can crack and short circuit. If that happens, the airbags can go off when they should not during a crash. Dealers will replace the seat weight sensors at no cost. This recall expands an earlier recall.

item.title: Honda Odyssey Side Air Bags May Deploy Unexpectedly
item.description: A software programming error in some Honda Odyssey minivans can cause the side air bags and side curtain air bags to deploy unexpectedly.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP Fuel Hose May Disconnect and Leak
item.description: On some Honda CB1000SP motorcycles, the hose that carries fuel to the engine may come loose from the fuel tank. This can cause fuel to leak out, including near the rear tire.

item.title: Honda CMX300/CMX500 Handlebar Lock Screw May Loosen
item.description: On certain Honda CMX300 and CMX500 motorcycles, the handlebar lock screw may gradually loosen and come loose from its mounting. If the screw detaches, it can become lodged between the frame and the steering stem. This can get in the way of normal steering, making the motorcycle harder to control and increasing the chance of a crash or injury for the rider.

item.title: Honda and Acura Driver Seats May Be Loose
item.description: Some Honda Accord, Accord Hybrid, HR-V, Pilot, and Acura Integra vehicles may have a driver's seat cushion frame that was not tightened properly. This can leave the seat loose. A loose driver's seat may not properly hold the driver in place during a crash, which increases the risk of injury.

item.title: Honda CBR650R Wiring May Cause Lighting Loss
item.description: American Honda is recalling certain 2024-2025 CBR650R motorcycles because engine vibration can damage the turn signal switch wiring. That damage can cause an electrical short and blow a fuse. If the fuse blows, the motorcycle can lose its turn signals, brake light, speedometer, and horn all at once.

item.title: Honda CBR600RR engine flaw risks rear wheel lockup
item.description: Some 2024-2026 Honda CBR600RR motorcycles may have a cylinder head that was not manufactured the way it should have been. This manufacturing problem can lead to a bearing on one of the engine's connecting rods failing. If that bearing fails, it may cause the motorcycle's rear wheel to suddenly lock up, or it may cause engine oil to leak out and land on the rear tire.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP Piston Defect Risks Rear Wheel Lockup
item.description: Some CB1000SP motorcycles have pistons and piston rings that may not have been manufactured correctly. This can lead to rod bearing failure, which can cause the rear wheel to lock up while riding, or cause engine oil to leak onto the rear tire.

item.title: Honda, Chrysler and Toyota Vans Wheelchair Restraint Issue
item.description: Some vehicles equipped with certain wheelchair restraint systems have retractors that may not lock properly. This means a wheelchair might not be securely held in place while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the retractors and replace them if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Honda Accord Hybrid Loss of Drive Power
item.description: Some Honda Accord Hybrid vehicles have a software problem in a computer that helps control the hybrid system. Because of this software error, that computer's processor may reset itself while you are driving. When the reset happens, the vehicle can suddenly lose the power that drives it forward. Losing drive power unexpectedly while on the road can catch a driver off guard.

item.title: Honda CB1000SP Gearshift Pedal Bolt May Loosen
item.description: Certain Honda CB1000SP Hornet SP motorcycles may have a problem with the pivot bolt on the gearshift pedal. This bolt could loosen over time and even detach completely, which would leave the rider unable to shift gears while riding. This means the motorcycle doesn't meet a federal safety standard covering motorcycle controls and displays. Dealers will replace the pivot bolt to fix this, free of charge.

item.title: Honda CRF1100 Loses Horn and High-Beam Switch
item.description: The wiring in the left handlebar switch pod can corrode from oxidation. When this happens, the horn may stop working, or the headlight may no longer switch between low beam and high beam. Either failure means the rider loses that control while riding, and the problem develops from corrosion inside the switch itself rather than from any outside damage to the motorcycle.

item.title: Acura, Honda Brake Pedal Pin Can Shift
item.description: The brake pedal in these vehicles is held in place by a pin that was not secured correctly. Because of this, the pedal can shift out of its normal position while the vehicle is being driven. When the pedal moves out of place, the driver may not be able to press the brakes the way they normally would, which can affect the vehicle's ability to slow down or stop.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid Fuel Hose May Leak Fuel
item.description: On certain 2025 Honda CR-V Hybrid vehicles, the fuel feed hose may not have been installed correctly. Because it wasn't installed the right way, fuel could leak out of the hose. As a result, these vehicles don't meet federal fuel system safety requirements. If fuel leaks and there's something nearby that could ignite it, this increases the risk of a fire.

item.title: Honda CMX1100, CRF1100, XL750 Oil Leak Risk
item.description: Certain Honda CMX1100, CRF1100 and XL750 motorcycles have a bolt problem in the engine. The bolt that seals the crankcase may not have been made correctly, which can let engine oil leak out and land on the rear tire. Oil on the rear tire may cause a loss of control while riding, which increases the risk of a crash or injury.

item.title: Honda CB300R headlight may flicker or fail
item.description: On certain CB300R motorcycles, the headlight may flicker or shut off completely while you are riding. Losing headlight illumination makes it harder for you and others to see, which raises the risk of a crash or injury. Dealers will replace the headlight assembly on affected motorcycles at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Honda ADV160 Scooter Oil Pump Gear Failure
item.description: Honda is recalling certain 2024 and 2025 ADV160 scooters. The oil pump driven gear may fail. If this gear fails, the scooter can lose drive power.

item.title: Honda CBR650R Gear Shift Arm May Loosen
item.description: On certain CB650R and CBR650R motorcycles, the fasteners holding the gear shift arm may loosen and come apart. This can make it impossible to shift gears while riding. Dealers will replace the gear shift arm, free of charge.

item.title: Honda Pilot third-row seat belt may not work
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Honda Pilot SUVs because the seat belt for the third-row passenger seat may not work. The belt was routed incorrectly, which traps it behind the passenger side panel so it cannot do its job. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule covering how people are protected in a crash. Dealers will inspect the seat belt routing and repair it if needed, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Acura MDX, TLX, Honda Pilot Engine May Stall
item.description: Certain Acura MDX Type-S, Acura TLX Type-S, and Honda Pilot vehicles have a software error in the fuel injection electronic control unit, sometimes called the FI-ECU. Because of this software error, the engine may stall or lose power while the vehicle is being driven.

item.title: Honda Pilot and Passport fuel filler pipe may leak
item.description: The tube that leads from the fuel filler opening to the gas tank, and the fuel filler pipe it connects to, may separate from each other on these Honda vehicles. When that happens, gasoline can leak out. Dealers will inspect the fuel filler neck tube and pipe and repair them as needed, at no charge. Owner notification letters were mailed January 7, 2025.

item.title: Honda CRF1100 Motorcycle Software Glitch May Stall Engine
item.description: Honda is recalling certain CRF1100 Africa Twin motorcycles because of a software error in the engine's fuel injection computer, known as the FI-ECU. This error is tied to a feature called Wheelie Control. When a rider turns that feature on, the software problem may cause the engine to stall or lose power while the motorcycle is being ridden. In short, riding with Wheelie Control switched on can make the fuel injection system act up, causing the engine to stop running or produce less power partway through a ride.

item.title: Honda and Acura Models Loose Driver's Seat Frame
item.description: In these vehicles, the frame underneath the driver's seat cushion may not have been tightened properly when the vehicle was built at the factory. Because the frame isn't properly tightened, the driver's seat can end up unsecured instead of being firmly fastened in place the way it should be. This means the seating system in these vehicles does not meet the federal safety standard that covers how seats must be secured.

item.title: Honda GL1800 Goldwing Primary Drive Gear Bolt May Break
item.description: Certain 2018 to 2021 Honda GL1800 Goldwing motorcycles have a bolt that secures the primary drive gear to the crankshaft. Over time, this bolt can break. If it breaks, the engine may stall while you are riding, and the rear wheel can lock up. An engine stall and a locked rear wheel happening together is a significant mechanical problem while the motorcycle is in motion.

item.title: Honda Accord and CR-V Hybrid Fuel Pump May Leak
item.description: Certain 2023-2024 Honda Accord and Accord Hybrid, 2023-2025 CR-V Hybrid, and 2025 Civic and Civic Hybrid vehicles have a high-pressure fuel pump that may crack. A cracked pump can leak fuel. This means fuel that should stay inside the fuel system can leak out instead, rather than being delivered to the engine the way it normally would.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid Battery May Spark or Lose Power
item.description: On certain Honda CR-V Hybrid vehicles, the high-voltage battery modules may not have been manufactured correctly. This can cause a terminal or connector inside the battery to break and spark, which increases the risk of injury or fire. The same problem can also cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power while you are driving, which increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Honda and Acura Steering Gearbox Can Cause Difficulty Steering
item.description: Honda says the steering gearbox in these vehicles may not have been manufactured correctly. This defect can create too much internal friction inside the gearbox assembly. That extra friction can make the steering feel harder to turn, so drivers may have more difficulty steering the vehicle than they should. Honda is recalling the vehicles to fix this steering gearbox problem so the issue is corrected properly.

item.title: Honda CR-V tires missing required date code marking
item.description: Honda is recalling certain 2024 CR-V vehicles because the identification number stamped on the tires is missing its four-digit date code. That code is part of the marking required by a federal safety standard for tires on light vehicles, so the tires as built do not meet that standard. Without the full number, an owner may not be able to tell whether their tires are covered by a safety recall. Dealers will inspect the tires and replace them if needed.

item.title: Honda Fit and HR-V rearview camera may not appear
item.description: Honda is recalling certain Fit and HR-V vehicles that were already part of an earlier recall. Because of a design problem in the power circuit for the audio display, the rearview camera picture may not come up on the screen when the engine is started with a key. These vehicles therefore do not meet the federal rear visibility standard. Vehicles that were repaired under the earlier recall still need this new repair done.

item.title: Honda Ridgeline rearview camera image may not display
item.description: The wire harness that connects the rearview camera to the vehicle's tailgate may fatigue over time and eventually break. If the harness breaks, the rearview camera image may stop displaying on the vehicle's screen. Without a working rearview camera, the driver has a reduced view of the area behind the vehicle. A reduced rear view increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Honda Passport, Ridgeline Steering Gearbox Can Loosen
item.description: Inside the steering gearbox is a ball joint housing that connects to the steering rack. On some of these vehicles, that housing can loosen and come apart from the rack. If the housing separates from the rack, you can lose the ability to steer the vehicle. Losing steering control while driving makes it much harder to keep the vehicle going where you want it to go, which raises the chance of a crash.

item.title: Honda CBR600RR, CBR1000RR, GL1800 Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: Certain Honda GL1800 Gold Wing, CBR600RR, and CBR1000RR motorcycles have a fuel pump impeller that may have been molded incorrectly. This can cause the impeller to deform, leading to fuel pump failure. If the fuel pump fails, the engine can stall while the motorcycle is being ridden.

item.title: Acura RDX and Odyssey Steering Corrosion Risk
item.description: On some Acura RDX and Honda Odyssey vehicles, the steering gear box may not have been tightened properly. This can let water get inside, causing corrosion and the gears to bind. Corroded, binding gears can make the steering harder to control.

item.title: Honda and Acura passenger seat sensor may crack
item.description: Honda is recalling certain 2020 through 2022 Honda and Acura vehicles, including Accord, Civic, CR-V, HR-V, Odyssey, Pilot, Passport, Ridgeline, Fit, Insight and the Acura MDX, RDX and TLX. The sensor that measures the weight of the person in the front passenger seat can crack and short out. When that happens, the system may not switch off the front passenger airbag when it is supposed to.

item.title: Honda and Acura Fuel Pump May Fail
item.description: In a wide range of Honda and Acura vehicles, the fuel pump located inside the fuel tank may fail. If it fails while you are driving, the engine can suddenly stall.

item.title: Honda CR-V Hybrid Battery Cable Fire Risk
item.description: On certain 2020-2022 CR-V Hybrid vehicles, a 12-volt battery cable that runs outside the vehicle's frame is missing a fuse on its power circuit. Without that fuse, the cable can short-circuit or overheat if the vehicle is involved in a crash. Honda is recalling these vehicles to correct this. The missing fuse means the power circuit for this cable does not have the protection it should have, which becomes a problem specifically if the vehicle experiences a crash.
